newsitem.title: USA: Starbucks says will meet '97 estimates - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Starbucks says will meet '97 estimates - Barron's.

text.p: Starbucks Corp chief financial officer Michael Casey said in Barron's June 9 issue that despite rising coffee prices, he expects the company to meet the current First Call earnings estimate of $0.70 per share for fiscal 1997, ending in September.
"We're in the process of building a global brand that's making us less dependent on the price of coffee," said Casey.

Coffee prices reached a twenty-year high in late May of $3.18 a pound, said the newspaper. But Casey told Barron's that coffee prices have averaged about $1.30 a pound over the past 50 years, and that "we feel confident that the price will drop below $2 or that we will have sufficient pricing flexibility" to maintain margins.
Casey added that despite concerns that Starbucks is opening too many outlets, there was still room for expansion.

"We're still opening stores in Washington, and we are highly penetrated there," he said. "We're not nearly penetrated in New York and New Jersey. We could build in New York for five more years without batting an eyelash."

The company is also expanding overseas, where it expects to have 200 stores in Asian markets by the year 2000. Those stores, said the company, are not expected to begin contributing to earnings until the next fiscal year.
